preconditions.description: The length n of the numbers is between 2 and 10^5 inclusive.
The input strings a and b both have exactly n digits.
Neither a nor b has a leading zero.

preconditions.expression: all('0' <= c <= '9' for c in a_str) and all('0' <= c <= '9' for c in b_str)
preconditions.description: All characters in a and b are valid decimal digits.

postconditions.expression: is_impossible or (is_valid_output and min_coins == c and len(moves) == min(min_coins, 100000))
postconditions.description: If impossible, output is -1. Otherwise, output contains the minimal coin count c, followed by the first min(c, 10^5) moves that transform a to b optimally.
The impossibility flag corresponds exactly to the case where no sequence of valid moves transforms a to b.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and all(1 <= d <= n - 1 and s in (1, -1) for d, s in moves)
postconditions.description: Each move in the output specifies a valid index d (1 to n-1) and a valid sign s (+1 or -1).

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and (c == 0 or (c > 0 and len(moves) == min(c, 100000)))
postconditions.description: The number of printed moves matches the required count, capped at 10^5.

postconditions.expression: not is_impossible and (c == 0 or (c > 0 and is_optimal_sequence(a_str, b_str, moves, c)))
postconditions.description: The sequence of moves transforms a to b using exactly c coins, and c is the minimal possible number of coins.
